deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page is the closing section of Riemann's student essay 'Versuch einer allgemeinen Auffassung der Integration und Differentiation', dated 14 Jan 1847 on the next page. In his notation Π(s)=Γ(s+1) and ψ(s)=d log Π(s)/ds = digamma(s+1). The essay's expression 1 defines, for ν<0,
  ∂^ν z = (1/Π(-ν-1)) ∫_k^x (x-t)^{-ν-1} z(t) dt + φ_ν.
Here φ_ν is the 'complementary function', a series Σ K_n (x-k)^{-ν-n}/Π(-ν-n). For ν≥0 one takes ∂^{ν-m} and differentiates m times.

Goal of the page. Find one explicit closed-form value of ∂^ν of particular functions; the general value then follows by adding φ_ν. The method is to bring x outside the integral sign. The first case is z=x^μ.

(a) μ>0 (the argument actually works for μ>-1). x^μ is continuous, so k=0 may be taken. Substitute t=xy:
  (1/Π(-ν-1)) ∫_0^x (x-t)^{-ν-1} t^μ dt = (x^{μ-ν}/Π(-ν-1)) ∫_0^1 (1-y)^{-ν-1} y^μ dy.
  The beta integral gives B(μ+1,-ν)/Γ(-ν) = Πμ/Π(μ-ν), so the value is Πμ/Π(μ-ν) · x^{μ-ν}.
  Its m-th derivative is Πμ/Π(μ-ν-m) · x^{μ-ν-m}. This equals ∂^{ν+m}x^μ by the definition for ν≥0. Hence for every ν:
  ∂^ν x^μ = Πμ/Π(μ-ν) · x^{μ-ν} + φ_ν.

(b) μ<0. x^μ is discontinuous at 0, so x and k must have the same sign. Integrate by parts m times, each time integrating the power of t and differentiating (x-t)^{a}.
  - Each step contributes the factor a/(μ+j) (mine).
  - The boundary terms at t=k are multiples of (x-k)^{-ν-j} and belong to φ_ν.
  - The boundary terms at t=x vanish as long as -ν-m>0.
  The result is
  (1/Π(-ν-1)) ∫_k^x (x-t)^{-ν-1} t^μ dt = Πμ/(Π(-ν-1-m) Π(μ+m)) ∫_k^x (x-t)^{-ν-1-m} t^{μ+m} dt + φ_ν.
  If -ν>-μ, one can choose m so that μ+m ≥ -1.
  - If μ+m>-1: ∫_0^k is counted in φ_ν, so the lower limit can be moved to 0. Case (a) applied to the reduced integral gives again Πμ/Π(μ-ν) · x^{μ-ν}. This holds for -ν>-μ, and by the rule ∂^{ν+1}z = d(∂^ν z)/dx it extends to all ν.
  - If μ+m=-1 (μ a negative integer): the exponent becomes -ν-1-m = μ-ν =: a. Split the integral:
    ∫_k^x (x-t)^a t^{-1} dt = x^a (log x - log k) + ∫_k^x ((x-t)^a - x^a)/t dt.
    The term -log k · x^a is of the form x^{-ν-n} with n=-μ, so it lies in φ_ν. Moving the lower limit to 0 costs another φ_ν term.
    Substituting t=x(1-y) gives x^a ∫_0^1 (y^a - y^0)/(1-y) dy.
    Riemann writes this as (ψ(μ-ν) - ψ0) x^{μ-ν}. So the value is the formal prefactor Πμ/(Π(μ-ν) Π(-1)) times [log x · x^{μ-ν} + (ψ(μ-ν) - ψ0) x^{μ-ν}]. This is formula 12 on the next page.
  - The page ends: generalize this by differentiation to all ν.
errors: Sign error in the final step. ∫_0^1 (y^a - 1)/(1-y) dy = -(ψ(a) - ψ(0)) = -(digamma(a+1) + EulerGamma). So the bracket should be log x - (ψ(μ-ν) - ψ0), not + (ψ(μ-ν) - ψ0). Example: a=1 gives the integral -1, while ψ(1)-ψ(0) = +1.

Consequence of the sign error: Riemann's constants are not 'corresponding' under differentiation. For f_a = x^a(log x + c_a)/Π(a) to satisfy f_a' = f_{a-1}, one needs c_{a-1} = c_a + 1/a. The correct sign c_a = -(ψ(a) - ψ0) satisfies this; Riemann's c_a = +(ψ(a) - ψ0) does not. The error carries over to formulas 12 and 14 on the next page. The correct form of 14 is the known x^{-ν}/Γ(1-ν) · (log x - γ - digamma(1-ν)).

The condition for the m-fold partial integration should be -ν-m>0: convergence at t=x and vanishing of the boundary terms there. The transcription's 'μ-ν-m>0' would be the wrong condition, though the image is ambiguous here.
Case (a) is stated for μ positive but holds for all μ>-1. This is harmless.

Placing ∫_0^k(...)dt and the -log k · x^a term into φ_ν relies on φ_ν being an infinite series in (x-k)^{-ν-n}. This is formal; convergence is not discussed. It is the well-known looseness of Riemann's complementary function.
The prefactor Πμ/Π(-1) for a negative integer μ is ∞/∞. Riemann leaves it formal (the next page acknowledges this). As a limit it equals (-1)^m/m! with m = -1-μ.

results.what: Fractional integral/derivative of a power: D^ν x^μ = Γ(μ+1)/Γ(μ-ν+1) · x^{μ-ν}, via the Euler beta integral
results.modern_name: Riemann–Liouville fractional derivative of a power function
results.usually_credited_to: Lacroix (1819) for the formula; Liouville (1832); the integral form to Abel/Liouville; Riemann's 1847 essay (published 1876) is standard history

results.what: Extension to negative non-integer μ by repeated partial integration, shifting the base point and absorbing terms into the complementary function
results.modern_name: Analytic continuation in μ of the Riemann–Liouville power formula

results.what: Case μ a negative integer: logarithmic term plus digamma constant, D^ν x^{-m-1} ∝ x^{μ-ν}(log x + const) with const involving ψ(μ-ν) - ψ(0)
results.modern_name: Fractional derivative of x^{-n} and of log x (digamma formula)

deep.surprise_reason: This is the published 1847 student essay 'Versuch einer allgemeinen Auffassung der Integration und Differentiation' (Werke 1876). Its content, including the power and logarithm formulas, is well known and attributed to Riemann. The only notable detail is the sign slip in the digamma term.

checkable.asserts: General beta-function identity behind the power formula
∫_0^1 (y^a-1)/(1-y)dy = -(ψ_R(a)-ψ_R(0)) for a=2 (value -3/2), showing Riemann's sign is wrong
The correctly signed constant (c_1=-1) gives consistent corresponding values: d/dx[x(log x - 1)] = log x; Riemann's sign would give x(log x + 1), whose derivative is log x + 2
Recurrence ψ_R(a)-ψ_R(a-1)=1/a used to test which sign makes the log-case values corresponding under differentiation

transcription_corrections: The condition after the partial-integration formula is likely '-ν-m>0' (mathematically required); the transcription's 'μ-ν-m>0' is doubtful.
'Exponent von t ⋛ -1' is likely '≧ -1' (greater than or equal to -1).
'explicite[?] Function x' is likely 'explicite Function von x'.
The first case says 'Ist μ positiv'; the formula Πμ/Π(μ-ν) x^{μ-ν} in the image is consistent with the transcription.
